Electrodeionization (EDI) is an advanced purification technology that continuously removes the trace amounts of ionic charge remaining in the permeate water exiting the reverse osmosis (RO) stage with the help of direct current (DC) electric field and selectively permeable ion exchange membrane/resin beds. Unlike classical mixed-bed deionization columns, in EDI modules, resins are continuously regenerated during operation with H⁺ and OH⁻ ions formed by the electrical dissociation of water. Thus, continuous production is ensured without the need for hazardous acid (HCl/H₂SO₄) and caustic (NaOH) storage, neutralization and regeneration stops.

Kondens dönüş hattında gelişen korozyon: The corrosion that develops in the condensate return line is caused not only from inside the boiler, but also from the bicarbonate/carbonate alkalinity in the feed water breaking down at high temperatures and carrying carbon dioxide (CO₂) with the steam. When the steam condenses, CO₂ passes back into the water phase, forming carbonic acid and rapidly lowering the condensate pH value.

The corrosion that develops in the condensate return line is caused not only from inside the boiler, but also from the bicarbonate/carbonate alkalinity in the feed water breaking down at high temperatures and carrying carbon dioxide (CO₂) with the steam. When the steam condenses, CO₂ passes back into the water phase, forming carbonic acid and rapidly lowering the condensate pH value. This acidic environment creates grooving, especially at the bottom of the pipe, thinning at threaded joints, and metal loss in low-flow pockets. Iron oxide (rust) particles mixed into the water as a result of corrosion in the line can be carried to the boiler with the return water and form dangerous iron scale on the hot boiler pipes.
